description: The tule of California's marshes: dense stands of round, leafless, dark green stems 1.5-3 m tall, firm and pithy, each with a small drooping tassel of brown spikelets just below the tip in summer. It grows in the shallow water of ponds and slow reaches, and its stems were the reed for houses, mats, boats and baskets of the native peoples of the valley and foothills.

season_notes.winter: Stems fade to grey-brown and many stand through the winter, leaning and broken.
season_notes.spring: New dark green stems shoot up from the rhizomes in the shallows.
season_notes.summer: Tall dark green stands; brown tassels of spikelets hang near the tips from June to September.
season_notes.fall: Stems yellowing to tan from the top; the seed drops into the water.

riparian.water: Rooted in mud under shallow, still or slow water most of the year, deeper than cattail tolerates (to about 1 m).

notes: Hardstem tule (Schoenoplectus acutus var. occidentalis; Scirpus acutus in older floras) is the dominant tule of California's freshwater marshes, ponds and slow river margins, from the valley into the mountains. Drawn by the emergent module: habit tule, a dense clump of round, upright, unbranched, leafless stems 1-3 m (leaves reduced to sheaths at the base), dark green and firm (hard-stemmed, with a spongy pith), 30 stems to a 1.2 m clump. The inflorescence comes out on the side of the stem a little below the tip (the stem's continuation is a bract), a loose cluster of brown, ovoid spikelets 7-15 mm that droops a little: heads shape tassel, June to September, brown. The stems stand through the winter grey-brown (height_by_month 0.85 then), many broken. It takes deeper water than cattail and often stands outside it in a pond (zones pond_margin 1.0; margin and the still pools of slow creeks less), orders [2, 7], permanence perennial. Compared with California bulrush (Schoenoplectus californicus) its stems are round, not obtusely three-angled, and darker, and its spikelets fewer and less clustered. Its stems were the reed of houses, mats, boats and duck decoys for the Miwok, Maidu, Nisenan and other peoples. Marsh birds and muskrats use it; none are in the game, so relations are empty. shades_water 0.1.
